configurePresets.name: nes-release
configurePresets.description: NES ROM via llvm-mos-sdk. Set LLVM_MOS_SDK to your SDK install root in local.cmake (copy local.cmake.example); CMakeLists.txt derives the MOS-aware toolchain from it so the IDE gets 6502 intelligence. The SDK does not need to be on PATH.

configurePresets.name: nes-pal-release
configurePresets.description: Same NES ROM build as nes-release, but TARGET_PLATFORM=nes_pal sets REGION=1 -- FamiStudio assembles with PAL note tables/timing instead of NTSC. See local.cmake.example for LLVM_MOS_SDK setup.

configurePresets.name: linux-release
configurePresets.description: Linux desktop build. Clang is enforced (not the host default gcc) so the ELF carries LLVM-flavoured DWARF that matches the llvm-mos NES toolchain's debug info. Both compilers are pinned: the engine is C++-only, but the SDL3 dependency enables C, and an unset CMAKE_C_COMPILER would fall back to gcc and mix toolchains in one binary. Absolute paths are deliberate: the llvm-mos SDK's bin dir is typically ahead of /usr/bin on PATH, so a bare 'clang++' resolves to the 6502 cross-compiler and links the desktop binary against NES crt0/link.ld.

configurePresets.name: linux-docker-release
configurePresets.description: Linux desktop build routed through the CLion Docker toolchain.

configurePresets.name: linux-x86-release
configurePresets.description: 32-bit Linux desktop build. Requires the i386/32-bit SDL3+libusb+ALSA dev packages plus the 32-bit crt/libstdc++/libgcc (g++-multilib on Debian, lib32-gcc-libs on Arch) that clang --target=i686-linux-gnu needs to link. CMakeLists.txt auto-detects which multiarch pkgconfig layout is present (Debian's /usr/lib/i386-linux-gnu/pkgconfig, Arch/openSUSE's /usr/lib32/pkgconfig) so this preset works both inside docker/Dockerfile.linux and natively on a 32-bit-capable host -- no hardcoded PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR needed here.

configurePresets.name: linux-arm64-release
configurePresets.description: 64-bit ARM (AArch64) Linux desktop build, e.g. for ARMv8/ARMv9 hosts. Targets the generic aarch64-linux-gnu baseline rather than pinning -march to a specific ARMv9 feature set, so the resulting binary runs on any 64-bit ARM Linux machine (ARMv8-A and up), not just ARMv9 silicon. Requires the aarch64 SDL3+libusb+ALSA dev packages for the host distro; when cross-compiling from x86_64, install the aarch64 cross toolchain and matching multiarch dev packages (gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu + libc6-dev-arm64-cross on Debian/Ubuntu) so clang can find aarch64 headers/libs.

configurePresets.name: win-x64-release
configurePresets.description: 64-bit Windows desktop build. Run inside a matching x64 MSVC developer environment (vcvarsall x64 / msvc-dev-cmd's default arch) so link.exe and the Windows SDK import libs match; CMAKE_C(XX)_COMPILER_TARGET pins clang to the x64 MSVC ABI triple explicitly rather than relying on clang's host-default target.

configurePresets.name: win-x86-release
configurePresets.description: 32-bit Windows desktop build. Run inside a matching x86 MSVC developer environment (vcvarsall x86 / msvc-dev-cmd's arch: x86) so link.exe and the Windows SDK import libs are 32-bit; CMAKE_C(XX)_COMPILER_TARGET is required here because clang otherwise defaults to the host's native x86_64 target regardless of which vcvarsall was loaded.

configurePresets.name: win-arm64-release
configurePresets.description: 64-bit ARM (AArch64) Windows desktop build, e.g. Surface Pro X / other Windows-on-ARM devices. Run inside a matching ARM64 MSVC developer environment (vcvarsall arm64 / msvc-dev-cmd's arch: arm64) so link.exe and the Windows SDK import libs match; CMAKE_C(XX)_COMPILER_TARGET pins clang to the arm64 MSVC ABI triple explicitly, the same way win-x64/win-x86 do for their own architectures.

configurePresets.name: mac-arm64-release
configurePresets.description: Apple Silicon (arm64) macOS build. CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES pins the architecture explicitly rather than relying on the host's default (which happens to be arm64 on an Apple Silicon Mac, but isn't guaranteed -- e.g. under Rosetta or on an Intel Mac cross-building for Apple Silicon).

configurePresets.name: mac-x64-release
configurePresets.description: Intel (x86_64) macOS build. CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES pins the architecture explicitly; building this on an Apple Silicon host cross-compiles via clang's built-in multi-arch support (no separate toolchain needed) but any FetchContent-built dependency (SDL3) is compiled for x86_64 too, so it still links and runs correctly under Rosetta 2.

configurePresets.name: ctr-release
configurePresets.description: Nintendo 3DS .3dsx via the devkitARM toolchain. Requires devkitPro installed and the DEVKITPRO env var set (e.g. /opt/devkitpro); the toolchain file pulls in libctru + citro2d/citro3d and the ctr_create_3dsx()/ctr_generate_smdh() helpers. CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME is set to Nintendo3DS by the toolchain, which drives the TARGET_CTR engine gating. The PICA200 has no paletted textures, so the backend renders the shared software PPU to one RGBA texture (like SDL) rather than a GPU tilemap (like GameCube/Wii).

configurePresets.name: gc-release
configurePresets.description: GameCube .dol via the devkitPPC toolchain. Requires devkitPro installed and the DEVKITPRO env var set (e.g. /opt/devkitpro); the toolchain file pulls in libogc + GX and the ogc_create_dol() helper. CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME is set to NintendoGameCube by the toolchain, which drives the TARGET_GC/TARGET_OGC engine gating.

configurePresets.name: wii-release
configurePresets.description: Wii .dol via the devkitPPC toolchain (also runs on Wii U via vWii). Requires devkitPro installed and the DEVKITPRO env var set (e.g. /opt/devkitpro); the toolchain file pulls in libogc + GX + WPAD and the ogc_create_dol() helper. CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME is set to NintendoWii by the toolchain, which drives the TARGET_WII/TARGET_OGC engine gating.

configurePresets.name: switch-release
configurePresets.description: Nintendo Switch .nro via the devkitA64 toolchain. Requires devkitPro installed and the DEVKITPRO env var set (e.g. /opt/devkitpro); the toolchain file pulls in libnx and the nx_generate_nacp()/nx_create_nro() helpers. CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME is set to NintendoSwitch by the toolchain, which drives the TARGET_NX engine gating. The backend rasterises the shared software PPU and CPU scale-blits it into the libnx framebuffer (no deko3d), with audout for music.

configurePresets.name: wiiu-release
configurePresets.description: Native Nintendo Wii U .rpx/.wuhb via the devkitPPC + wut toolchain (NOT vWii -- this is a native Cafe OS app). Requires devkitPro installed with wut + the wiiu-sdl2 portlib and the DEVKITPRO env var set (e.g. /opt/devkitpro); the toolchain file pulls in wut and the wut_create_rpx()/wut_create_wuhb() helpers. CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME is set to CafeOS by the toolchain, which drives the TARGET_WIIU engine gating. The backend rasterises the shared software PPU into an SDL2 streaming texture the GPU scales to the window, with SDL2 audio for music.

configurePresets.name: nds-release
configurePresets.description: Nintendo DS .nds via the devkitARM toolchain. Requires devkitPro installed and the DEVKITPRO env var set (e.g. /opt/devkitpro); the toolchain file (NDS.cmake) pulls in libnds + calico and the nds_create_rom() helper. CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME is set to NintendoDS by the toolchain, which drives the TARGET_NDS engine gating. Unlike the SDL-style software-framebuffer backends, the DS backend maps the NES PPU onto the console's native 2D hardware: CHR -> char VRAM, nametable -> BG tilemap, OAM shadow -> hardware OBJ, and the raster band timeline -> a per-scanline HBlank scroll table (so sprite-0 splits still work). The 256x192 panel shows a window onto the full 256x240 NES world; the NES game is never altered for the DS.

configurePresets.name: dsi-release
configurePresets.description: Nintendo DSi .nds via the devkitARM toolchain -- same libnds 2D-hardware backend as the DS preset, but built with the DSi extensions enabled (TARGET_DSI). The DSi's larger RAM (16 MB vs 4 MB) and faster clock let the build attempt to embed crunched audio; when that does not fit, it falls back to the same user-supplied/stubbed audio path as the DS. Requires devkitPro installed and the DEVKITPRO env var set; the toolchain file (NDS.cmake) pulls in libnds + calico and the nds_create_rom() helper.
